notes: Wellmann III 110 (page header 'III 109, 2. 110', p. 121). The chapter covers two kinds: the mountain kind (ὀρεινόν, also called τεύθριον) and a second, more shrubby and weaker kind. Dimopoulos et al. 2013, Appendix III: 'Teucrium polium s.str. is confined to the W Mediterranean area and in Greece is replaced by T. capitatum (Greuter & al. 1986: 376)'. Earlier Greek records of T. polium refer to T. capitatum. Model on GBIF speciesKey 7308670 (Teucrium capitatum), not 3887764 (T. polium). Checklist entry: 'Teucrium capitatum L.', present in all 13 Greek floristic regions, chorology Me, not endemic.

excerpt: κάππαρις· οἱ δὲ κυνόσβατον, οἱ δὲ καπρίαν, οἱ δὲ κόρακος μῆλον, […] θάμνος ἐστὶν ἀκανθώδης, ἐπὶ γῆς γυροειδῶς ἐστρωμένος, ἀκάνθας ἀγκιστροειδεῖς ἔχων ὡς βάτος
excerpt_edition: Wellmann, Pedanii Dioscuridis Anazarbei De materia medica, vol. I (Berlin 1907), p. 240; read off the archive.org page image (item b21459162_0001; the OCR of this volume is not usable Greek); ϑ printed as θ
notes: Wellmann II 173 (p. 240). Taxonomic caveat: Dimopoulos et al. 2013 splits Greek capers into C. orientalis Veill. (most regions), C. sicula Veill. and C. zoharyi Inocencio & al. It lists C. spinosa L. s.str. with '?' in most regions and comments that it is a hybridogenous nothotaxon, mainly cultivated or feral (Inocencio & al. 2006). WCVP (and therefore POWO) instead treats all of these within C. spinosa: C. orientalis is a synonym of C. spinosa subsp. rupestris, C. sicula of var. canescens and C. zoharyi of subsp. aegyptia. C. spinosa s.l. is native in Greece, Kriti and the East Aegean. GBIF caveat: the backbone treats C. sicula, C. zoharyi and C. rupestris as synonyms of C. spinosa (speciesKey 6370689), but C. orientalis Duhamel as a SEPARATE accepted species (speciesKey 5601705). Greek occurrence records may therefore be split, and the pipeline should consider merging key 5601705.

evidence.claim: Dimopoulos et al. 2013 Capparaceae entries and Appendix III comment on C. spinosa s.str.
GBIF backbone: Capparis orientalis accepted, key 5601705

excerpt_edition: Wellmann, Pedanii Dioscuridis Anazarbei De materia medica, vol. I (Berlin 1907), p. 228; read off the archive.org page image (item b21459162_0001; the OCR of this volume is not usable Greek); ϑ printed as θ
notes: Wellmann II 164 (p. 228). Wellmann's II 165 is a second kyklaminos (κυκλάμινος ἑτέρα), not this species; Sprengel 1829 numbers that chapter II 194. The ivy-like, variegated leaves fit both C. hederifolium and C. graecum. Choosing C. graecum is provisional: no philological source was opened to support it over C. hederifolium. Neither is a Greek endemic, though C. graecum subsp. candicum is range-restricted to Kriti. If the identification literature favours C. hederifolium (GBIF speciesKey 7127810), switch to it.
